verdict.rationale: Foreloop's docs say a plain-language description such as "Users can't tell which invoices are overdue" is enough to start an intention, with no need to know which files change. Its agent then reads the input, fills in the intention and proposes the tasks, which become approvable task contracts with editable deliverables. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, explicit documentation of how task scope is bounded when a developer (rather than an end-user report) starts the intention.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have it automatically turned into a scoped implementation task

citations.quote: "Users can't tell which invoices are overdue" is enough to start; you do not need to know which files change.
its agent reads the submission, fills in the intention, and proposes the tasks
An intention adds an agreed purpose and editable deliverables when you need more clarity.
Nothing runs until a person approves a contract.
